title: Dispatch parallel agents on tiny fixes with hard 5-min time limit

summary: Launch phase 0: multiple parallel agents, each fixing ONE tiny issue, hard stop at 5 minutes per agent.
impact: Validates rapid-turnaround agent model; forces scope discipline; quick wins build momentum.

title: Minimize test cases, use debugging tools

summary: Instructs to keep test case reproduction minimal and leverage existing debugging tools rather than ad-hoc approaches.
impact: Constrains investigative work to focused, efficient patterns; prioritizes existing tool use over manual debugging.

title: Address underlying design; no shortcuts allowed

summary: Rejects expedient fixes in favor of proper architectural solutions; establishes quality bar against quick-patch mentality.
impact: Enforces architectural rigor in all fixes; prevents technical debt accumulation; fixes must address root causes not symptoms.

title: Fix basic behaviors first; unlock more tests

summary: Prioritizes foundational engine correctness (Object methods, Array methods) before advanced ES6 features (destructuring, generators).
impact: Backlog ordering: basic builtins are prerequisites for advanced features; fixes here unlock test262 phase progression.

title: Engine is strict-only; remove all sloppy paths

summary: Declares the engine will support ES5/ES6 strict mode only; requires comprehensive audit and removal of all sloppy-mode code paths.
impact: Fundamental architecture constraint; eliminates arguments.caller, implicit globals, sloppy eval; greatly simplifies engine model.

title: Give agents smaller, scoped investigation tasks

summary: Corrects over-scoped task assignment; agent was debugging when it should have been analyzing; requests tighter scope boundaries.
impact: Process rule: agent tasks must be narrowly scoped and time-bounded; exploration + debugging in same task causes scope creep.

title: Agent task scope must be reduced and focused
quote: you can use agents to do basic analysis, just make sure they have a reduced scope
summary: Confirms agents can assist with analysis but scope must remain narrow; prevents task expansion beyond stated boundaries.
impact: Process rule: agent tasks bound to single root cause, single file, or single feature; no cross-cutting architectural work.

title: Rosetta suite requires full pass with zero flakiness
quote: now start work on the follow-ups. dispatch agents to work on small tasks. and I want full pass on the rosetta tests, there is no room for flakyness as the engine should be fully determinitisc
summary: Establishes rosetta as quality gate with zero tolerance for nondeterminism; all tests must pass consistently, no flaky workarounds.
impact: Quality bar: rosetta is regression baseline; engine must be fully deterministic; no workarounds for intermittent failures.

title: Verify no duplicate definitions removed
quote: did you remove the duplicated definitions? are they defined somewhere else? double check
summary: Questioned whether duplicate definitions were safely removed; required verification they exist elsewhere.
impact: Prevented silent loss of functionality; enforced verification before cleanup commits.

title: Declare full ES6+ syntax support required

summary: Declared that destructuring, default parameters, spread, and async/await are non-optional features; required scope documentation.
impact: Broadened scope to cover modern ES6+ syntax; established as requirements for the engine, not optional extras.

title: Prioritize basic engine behaviors over test count
quote: check BACKLOG.md for tasks that make sense to address - we need to fix the basic behaviours of the engine first to unlock more tests
summary: Redirected focus from raw test count to foundational behavior fixes; prioritized unblocking over volume.

title: Discriminate determinism from regressions
quote: The root cause is heap pollution in the batch worker process — the __resetGlobals() / hp.reset() / vm_reset() cycle doesn't fully restore all mutable heap state between tests, causing non-deterministic ordering-dependent failures.
summary: Identified that apparent regressions (232 tests PASS→FAIL) were actually non-determinism: 256 tests also changed FAIL→PASS in same period. Net loss only 11 tests, not 211. Root cause: batch test runner heap pollution from prototype mutations.
impact: Clarified that test262 failures are ordering-dependent pollutants, not logic errors in array.c3 fixes. Requires worktrace-level reset strategy, not code fixes.

title: Historical test262 tracking via git mining

summary: Directed extraction of test262 pass counts from project git history (commit messages, progress.md snapshots, plan files) for all dates since project start, using agents to work in parallel worktrees by date range.
impact: Established metrics pipeline to track test262 pass rate trajectory and validate performance claims without re-running full suite. Constraint: use historical records only, no new test execution.

title: Priority feature identification discipline

summary: Requested structured ranking of next high-value features and delegation of feature identification work to haiku agents for efficiency.
impact: Shifted feature pipeline planning to agents. Establishes pattern: haiku agents for feature assessment, prioritization, and small edits.

summary: Directed focus on bugs B37 and B39 using structural (not quick-fix) methodology: minimal test cases as guide, validation, and atomic commits per fix.

impact: Quality bar: unsupported feature tests must be pre-skipped, not run and counted as CE. Affects test262 baseline interpretation and pass-rate accounting.

title: Task dependency injection: build as dep

summary: Architecture decision: build should be a task dependency, not an inline c3c build command call. Use the task system's dependency mechanism.
impact: Harness efficiency: avoids redundant builds by leveraging task DAG tracking. Builds only when sources change.

title: Deep code review on destructuring
quote: In the file /Users/rtomasi/cousas/duktape-c3/src/compiler/statements.c3, I need to understand: 1. The ArrayBind and ObjBind struct definitions...5. The compile_catch_object_pattern() function around line 4133-4171
summary: Requested detailed code review targeting destructuring semantics: ArrayBind/ObjBind structs, for_statement destructuring path, iterator-loop emit, and catch-pattern compilation.
impact: Focused investigation into destructuring codegen to identify how catch-clause path differs from function-param path (which has bugs). Root-cause analysis before fix.

title: Iterator protocol for function-param destructuring
quote: Reproduced the bug: function f([a,b]){} called with a generator produces undefined undefined instead of 1 2. Root-caused: the function-param destructuring in functions.c3 uses LDINT index + GETPROP src, index (direct indexed property access) instead of the iterator protocol
summary: Root-cause analysis for B37: function-param destructuring uses direct property access (LDINT+GETPROP) instead of iterator protocol. Catch-clause already uses correct protocol. Three emission sites affected.
impact: Architecture gap identified: function-param destructuring and catch-clause destructuring diverged. Requires unifying on iterator protocol across all three emission sites (regular, inner, arrow functions).

title: No quick-fix culture: structural fixes only
quote: fix all underlying issues you find. we dont care for 'quick fixes'. do it right and be methodical.
summary: Reinforced quality bar: all fixes must be structural and methodical, not tactical. Address root causes, not symptoms.
impact: Constraint on work discipline: no time-pressure shortcuts; all changes must reflect underlying correctness.

title: 100% test262 pass rate goal (with perf constraints)

summary: Goal set: achieve 100% pass rate on test262 targeted subset without performance regressions. Stop hook enforces goal until met.
impact: Hard constraint on sessions: must reach 100% test262 pass rate. Perf constraint prevents optimizations that trade correctness for speed. Goal drives all work.

title: Async function compilation flag loss
quote: The bug is in the compiler, not the runtime. Async functions are being compiled with flags.is_async = false despite being declared with async: ...flags.is_async=false while flags.is_generator=true is exactly the shape of a function* (generator without async), not async function
summary: Root-cause of async/await failures: compiler losing is_async flag during function compilation. Flag restoration/save ordering bug in compile_inner_function likely culprit.
impact: Identified compiler bug, not runtime. Async functions treated as generators (allocate GENERATOR HObject instead of Promise). Requires flag-tracking fix in statements.c3 or functions.c3.

title: ArrayBuffer/TypedArray/DataView implementation

impact: Feature scope: binary data types as prerequisite for higher test262 pass rate. Process constraint: limit agent spawn depth to 1.

title: JIT architecture: platform-agnostic encoder design

summary: Established architectural principle for JIT implementation: minimize scope to hot paths, separate arch-specific encoders from core compiler to enable multi-platform support (arm64 + x86-64)
impact: Guided JIT design to avoid monolithic architecture; enables future backends by isolating platform-specific code from compilation logic

summary: Questioned and documented intended advantage of refcounting: immediate deallocation for UI rendering workloads vs GC pause accumulation at 60fps
impact: Clarified performance objective; refcount immediate-dealloc should motivate architectural designs

title: Question refcount API: RAII alternatives to manual decref

title: Investigate O(n) random-access alternatives across ecosystems

impact: Scoped architectural research to inform future design choices; comparative-language approach to baseline validation

title: Strict-only engine: skip sloppy-mode tests
quote: The engine is strict-only. These `onlyStrict` tests test sloppy-mode behavior and can never pass.
summary: Establish that strict mode is the engine's permanent operational mode. Skip-list all `onlyStrict` tests that expect sloppy-mode behavior.
impact: Clarifies the engine's scope: do not implement or fix sloppy-mode semantics. Reduces test262 churn from unfixable sloppy-mode failures.

title: Private field semantics: bypass proxy traps
quote: Private field access should NOT go through proxy's get trap. Per ES2022 spec, PrivateFieldGet does NOT call [[Get]] — it directly looks up the private field.
summary: Ensure private field get/set bypasses proxy traps entirely. Fix evaluation order: RHS getter runs before membership check. Add extensibility check for non-extensible objects.
impact: Fixes 7+ test262 failures related to private field semantics. Aligns engine behavior with ES2022 spec for private slots.

title: Proxy constructor: accept lightfunc targets

summary: Extend Proxy validation to allow built-in functions (lightfuncs) as valid Proxy targets, not just HObjects.
impact: Unblocks 5 test262 tests that create proxies wrapping built-in functions like Math.max or Array.isArray.

title: Eval inherits super and new.target from caller
quote: Eval code inside a method should inherit the super binding from the enclosing method. The eval code should be able to use `super.property` to access the parent prototype.
summary: Enable eval to access caller's super binding and new.target. Fix SyntaxError vs TypeError distinctions for super/new.target at different context levels.
impact: Fixes 10+ test262 failures in eval-code tests for super and new.target handling across function and non-function contexts.

title: TypedArray must NOT look up Symbol.species

summary: Fix TypedArray constructor to skip Symbol.species lookup for same-typed-array sources. Use spec's ArraySpeciesCreate correctly.
impact: Fixes test262 failures for TypedArray-to-TypedArray construction without triggering unnecessary species lookup.

title: Use shared ArrayIteratorPrototype.next
quote: TypedArray construction from array should use the shared ArrayIteratorPrototype.next method.
summary: Ensure TypedArray constructor iteration uses the standard shared iterator protocol, allowing iterator modifications to affect construction.
impact: Enables proper observable iterator behavior in TypedArray construction; allows test code to verify iterator trap execution.

title: Enforce extensibility in indirect eval

summary: Indirect eval must respect global object extensibility. Throw TypeError for var/function declarations on non-extensible globals.
impact: Ensures eval respects object extension invariants; correct semantics for sealed/frozen global object scenarios.
